stem: Which entry writes off an irrecoverable (bad) debt owed by a customer?

options.content: Debit irrecoverable debts; credit the customer's account
options.rationale: Correct: an expense, and the debt is removed.

options.content: Debit the customer's account; credit irrecoverable debts
options.rationale: This is the reverse entry (used to reinstate a debt).

options.content: Debit sales; credit the customer's account
options.rationale: Sales are not reduced by bad debts.

options.content: Debit irrecoverable debts; credit bank
options.rationale: No cash is paid when a debt is written off.

explanation: The expense account is debited and the customer is credited to clear the debt.

stem: Which accounting concept is the main reason for writing off irrecoverable debts?

options.content: Going concern
options.rationale: Going concern is about the business continuing.

options.content: Duality
options.rationale: Duality explains the two entries, not the reason.

options.content: Prudence
options.rationale: Correct: assets must not be overstated, and known losses are recognised.

options.content: Realisation
options.rationale: Realisation is about when revenue is recognised.

explanation: Keeping an uncollectable debt would overstate trade receivables and profit.

stem: What is the effect of writing off an irrecoverable debt of US\$500?

options.content: Profit falls by US\$500; cash falls by US\$500
options.rationale: No cash moves when a debt is written off.

options.content: Profit and trade receivables both fall by US\$500
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Trade receivables fall by US\$500; profit is unchanged
options.rationale: The write-off is an expense, so profit falls.

options.content: Sales and trade receivables both fall by US\$500
options.rationale: Sales are not changed.

explanation: Expense up 500 (profit down 500); trade receivables down 500; cash unchanged.

stem: A debt of US\$720 written off last year is received in full this year. What is the **first** entry under the recommended method?

options.content: Debit bank; credit irrecoverable debts recovered
options.rationale: This skips reinstating the customer's account.

options.content: Debit bank; credit the customer
options.rationale: This is the second entry.

options.content: Debit irrecoverable debts recovered; credit the customer
options.rationale: This is the reverse of the reinstatement.

options.content: Debit the customer; credit irrecoverable debts recovered
options.rationale: Correct: reinstate the debt before recording the receipt.

explanation: Reinstate first so the customer's record shows the debt was eventually paid; then debit bank, credit the customer.

stem: A customer owing US\$3,600 is declared bankrupt and pays 35 cents in the dollar in full and final settlement. How much is written off?

options.rationale: This is the amount received.
Part of the debt was paid, so not all of it is written off.
Correct: 65% of 3,600.
35 cents in the dollar means 35%, not 35 dollars.

stem: After the trial balance was prepared, a further debt of US\$290 was found to be irrecoverable. Which pair of adjustments is needed in the financial statements?

options.content: Add 290 to irrecoverable debts in the income statement and deduct 290 from cash at bank
options.rationale: Cash is not affected.

options.content: Deduct 290 from sales and from trade receivables
options.rationale: Sales are not reduced.

options.content: Deduct 290 from trade receivables only
options.rationale: The expense must also be recognised.

options.content: Add 290 to irrecoverable debts in the income statement and deduct 290 from trade receivables
options.rationale: Correct: the adjustment affects both statements.

explanation: Expense up 290 and trade receivables down 290.
hints: Every year-end adjustment is used twice.

stem: Why does the recommended method reinstate a recovered debt in the customer's account before recording the cash?

options.content: Because cash can only be credited to an expense account
options.rationale: Cash is credited to the customer, not an expense.

options.content: So the customer's account shows a full history, including that the debt was paid
options.rationale: Correct: useful if the customer later asks for credit.

options.content: To increase the total of trade receivables shown at the year end
options.rationale: Trade receivables end up unchanged: debit and credit cancel.

options.content: Because the recovered amount must be added to sales
options.rationale: Recoveries are other income, not sales.

explanation: Reinstatement keeps a complete record of the customer's payment history.
hints: Think about what the credit controller sees in the account.

stem: Writing off an irrecoverable debt reduces the business's bank balance.
explanation: False. No money is paid; the debt is simply removed.

stem: Irrecoverable debts recovered are shown as other income (or deducted from irrecoverable debts) in the income statement.
explanation: True. The recovery increases profit in the year it is received.

stem: Match each event with its double entry.

left.content: Year-end transfer of debts written off

right.content: Dr Income statement, Cr Irrecoverable debts
Dr Customer, Cr Irrecoverable debts recovered

explanation: Write-off, reinstatement, receipt and closing transfer.

payload.template: A debt that will certainly not be paid is {{blank:a}}; a debt that might not be paid is {{blank:b}}. Only the first kind is written off.

explanation: Doubtful debts are covered by an allowance (provision); irrecoverable debts are written off.

stem: Trade receivables at 31 December 2025 were US\$18,650 before two debts of US\$430 and US\$1,125 were written off. What are trade receivables after the write-offs?

Nyasha's gross profit for 2025 was US\$23,480 and her other expenses were US\$14,260. During the year she wrote off irrecoverable debts of US\$980 and recovered US\$340 from a customer whose debt had been written off in 2023. Calculate her profit for the year.
explanation: 23,480 + 340 − 14,260 − 980 = 8,580. Treating the recovery as an expense gives 7,900.
workedSolution: 1. 23,480 + 340 − 14,260 − 980 = 8,580. Treating the recovery as an expense gives 7,900.
hints: A recovery is income; a write-off is an expense.

stem: Give **two** situations in which a business would write off a customer's debt as irrecoverable.

points.description: The customer is bankrupt / has gone out of business with no assets
The customer has died with no estate, or cannot be traced / has left the country

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: When the customer is declared bankrupt and cannot pay, and when the customer cannot be traced after leaving the area.

explanation: A debt is written off only when there is no realistic chance of payment.

stem: Sipho does not want to write off a debt of US\$2,100 owed by a customer who has left the country, because 'it will make my profit look worse'. Advise him.

points.description: He should write it off: the debt will not be received, so it is not an asset
Keeping it overstates trade receivables and profit (prudence)
Users would be misled / he might take drawings based on a profit that does not exist

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Sipho should write the debt off. It cannot be collected, so leaving it in trade receivables overstates assets and profit, breaking the prudence concept. He and the bank would be misled and he might withdraw money the business never had.

explanation: A true and fair view needs the loss to be recognised.
hints: Which concept requires losses to be recognised?

stem:
Rudo sells electrical goods on credit in Gweru. During 2025:

| Date | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 10 Mar | Mutsa Hardware, owing US\$1,870, was declared bankrupt. A final payment of 25 cents in the dollar was received by bank transfer and the rest was written off. |
| 28 Jun | Banda Contractors, owing US\$655, could not be traced. The debt was written off. |
| 5 Oct | Zuva Electrical paid US\$1,240 by bank transfer. This debt had been written off in 2024. |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount written off for Mutsa Hardware.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Prepare journal entries to record the three events. Narratives are required.

points.description: 10 Mar: Dr Bank 467.50 and Dr Irrecoverable debts 1,402.50
28 Jun: Dr Irrecoverable debts 655, Cr Banda Contractors 655
5 Oct: Dr Zuva Electrical 1,240, Cr Irrecoverable debts recovered 1,240
5 Oct: Dr Bank 1,240, Cr Zuva Electrical 1,240

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Journal**

| Date | Details | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 10 Mar 2025 | Bank | 467.50 |  |
|  | Irrecoverable debts | 1,402.50 |  |
|  | Mutsa Hardware |  | 1,870 |
|  | *Final dividend of 25 cents in the dollar received; balance written off* |  |  |
| 28 Jun 2025 | Irrecoverable debts | 655 |  |
|  | Banda Contractors |  | 655 |
|  | *Debt written off: customer cannot be traced* |  |  |
| 5 Oct 2025 | Zuva Electrical | 1,240 |  |
|  | Irrecoverable debts recovered |  | 1,240 |
|  | *Debt written off in 2024 reinstated* |  |  |

|  | Zuva Electrical |  | 1,240 |
|  | *Amount received from Zuva Electrical* |  |  |

parts.explanation: Reinstate the recovered debt before recording the receipt.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the amount transferred from the irrecoverable debts account to the income statement for 2025.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the irrecoverable debts account for 2025.

points.description: Debits: Mutsa Hardware 1,402.50 and Banda Contractors 655

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
**Irrecoverable debts account**

| Date | Details | US\$ | Date | Details | US\$ |

| 28 Jun 2025 | Banda Contractors | 655 |  |  |  |
|  |  | **2,057.50** |  |  | **2,057.50** |

parts.explanation: The recovery is in a separate account.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate the net effect of these events on Rudo's profit for 2025. Enter the amount by which profit is reduced.

explanation: This item practises writing off and recovering debts.

stem: Thandeka's trial balance at 31 December 2025 included trade receivables US\$26,840 and irrecoverable (bad) debts US\$1,150. Gross profit was US\$31,250 and other expenses were US\$18,930. After the trial balance was prepared, she learned that a customer owing US\$760 had died with no estate.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the irrecoverable debts expense for the year.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate trade receivables to be shown in the statement of financial position.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the US\$760 is written off now rather than when the customer's estate is finally closed.

points.description: It is already known the debt will not be received
Prudence: losses are recognised as soon as they are known, so assets and profit are not overstated

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The loss is already certain, and prudence requires known losses to be recognised immediately so that trade receivables and profit are not overstated.

explanation: This item practises a year-end write-off.
hints: A late write-off changes both the expense and trade receivables.
